data.falsifier: a drifted route fact beats a verified model fact, or unknown model not named

data.reason: internal pure service with no consumer-visible command yet; README unaffected

chunk_findings.detail: When `model` is already a mapping and `route` is a route name (`str`), `effective` leaves `route` as a `str`. `_layer_tables` then runs `(route or {}).get("facts", {})`, which calls `.get` on a `str` and raises `AttributeError`. Example: `effective({"id":"h","facts":{}}, {"id":"m","family":"f","facts":{},"family_facts":{}}, "r", catalog=catalog)`. The signature explicitly allows `route: Mapping | str`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/combine.py:_layer_tables

chunk_findings.detail: When `model` is a `str` and `route` is an explicit route mapping, the branch passes `None` as the route name to `model_layer`, then overwrites `route` with the catalog-derived route. This silently discards the caller-supplied route facts. Example: `effective({"id":"h","facts":{}}, "m", {"id":"r","facts":{"long_context": {"v": True, "s":"verified"}}}, catalog=catalog)` loses the route override. That makes the route layer fail exactly when a caller supplies it as a mapping.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/combine.py:effective

chunk_findings.detail: The sparse pair table is not consumed by `effective`: `match_pair` is never called, and `_layer_tables` assigns `pair` directly to `tables["pair"]`. If `pair` is the sparse `[[pair]]` row list documented by `match_pair`, `_layer_tables` places a `list` in `tables["pair"]`, and `_ordinary`/`_safety` then call `.get` on it, raising `AttributeError`. Example pair: `[{"harness":"h","model":"m","facts":{"long_context": {"v": True, "s":"verified"}}}]`. The route×model pair override is therefore never applied.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/combine.py:effective

chunk_findings.detail: This test promised for the Copilot long_context tier never uses `long_context` at all: the pair row has `price_in=F(2.0)` and the effective call requests only `keys=["price_in"]`. A `combine.effective` implementation that completely mishandles the Copilot long_context tier would still pass this test, because the only asserted field is `price_in`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_combine.py:test_copilot_long_context_pair_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The observed fact is `F(2, "verified")` while the operator fact is `F(1)`, which uses the default `"documented"` status. The assertion `a["window"] == 2` can therefore be satisfied by status precedence (`verified` beats `documented`) even if the implementation wrongly ranks `operator` above `observation`. The test does not isolate the required `observation > operator` source precedence.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_combine.py:test_observation_beats_operator_and_deterministic

chunk_findings.detail: Safety caps are discarded when no ordinary fact exists. In `_resolve_key`, the `got is None` branch returns the LCD value before the `caps` list is ever computed. Given tables with `cap.max_tokens` as a verified fact value `1000` and no `max_tokens` fact, and `Policy(lcd={"max_tokens": 4000})`, `effective(..., keys=["max_tokens"])` returns `4000`, above the safety cap `1000`. This violates the rule "every `cap.<key>` tightens `<key>` by `min`" and can let a consumer exceed a safety bound.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/combine.py:_resolve_key

chunk_findings.detail: `route` is declared `Mapping | str | None`, but a route name is only converted when `model` is also a `str`. If `model` is a mapping and `route` is `"openai"`, `_layer_tables` does `(route or {}).get("facts", {})` on a `str` and crashes with `AttributeError`. Conversely, if `model` is a `str` and `route` is a mapping, the mapping is silently passed to `model_layer` as `None`, so all route facts are dropped and the wrong layer can win.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/combine.py:effective

chunk_findings.detail: The sparse pair table promised by the intent and documented by `match_pair` is never used by `effective`: `_layer_tables` stores the `pair` argument verbatim as `"pair": pair or {}`, and `match_pair` is dead code. Passing a sparse pair row list such as `[{"harness": "h", "model": "m", "facts": {...}}]` makes `_ordinary` call `.get` on a `list` (or `_all_keys` call `.startswith` on a row dict) and raises `AttributeError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/combine.py:_layer_tables

chunk_findings.detail: The intended scenario is "Copilot long_context tier", but this test never supplies or asserts a `long_context` fact. It only creates a pair override for `price_in` and checks `price_in`. An implementation that completely fails to apply the Copilot long_context pair-tier override to `long_context` would still pass this test, so the required scenario is not actually exercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_combine.py:test_copilot_long_context_pair_tier
